hero.eyebrow: Haus Till E on the Moselle loop in Zell
hero.sub: In our listed Art Deco house with its own history, five individual double rooms full of charm and character await you. Start the day with a delicious breakfast in our cosy breakfast room – before losing track of time in our wildly romantic garden.

text: Once upon a time there was a castle owner who had three daughters – and he bequeathed each of them a part of the Zell castle, built in the 16th century: to one the side wing, to another the main building, and for the third he had a new building erected that blends harmoniously in style and character into the castle ensemble.

What sounds like a fairy tale is a true story from the 1920s in Zell. This is how the estate came into being that is known and cherished today as Haus Till E. Our listed building dates from the Art Deco era and has been lovingly restored in the style typical of that period. Windows, doors, wooden floors and the staircase are all original and give the house its unique flair.

In front of the house awaits a wildly romantic, idyllic garden. Over a bottle of wine, you can let your soul unwind here and lose all sense of time, before diving back into the story of these old walls.

accordion.title: Directions
accordion.content: Haus Till E is a short walk from the Moselle, right in the heart of Zell's old town, on Schloßstraße. Coming from Bullay, you cross the Moselle via the road bridge and drive through Merl into Zell's old town. Other routes lead via the Zeller Berg and Grenderich (L199), through the Altlay valley (L194), or from Kappel via the B421. By train, you can reach us via Bullay's 'Umweltbahnhof' – from there, the bus takes you about 3 km to the Lindenplatz stop, just a short walk from Haus Till E. The nearest airport is Frankfurt-Hahn (approx. 20 km). Whether arriving by train or plane, just let us know – we're happy to pick you up by car.

accordion.title: Address
accordion.content: You'll find Haus Till E at Schloßstraße 10, 56856 Zell (Moselle) – right at the foot of the steep vineyard 'Zeller Schwarze Katz', just a few minutes' walk from the Moselle promenade and the old town.

accordion.title: Parking
accordion.content: Along the Moselle riverside there are numerous free parking spaces. Right on Schloßstraße you can park with a pay-and-display ticket – for loading and unloading your luggage, the free 30-minute ticket is usually enough. From early 2027, we'll also offer our own garage parking spaces right at the house.

accordion.title: Pets
accordion.content: We both love dogs dearly – but over the years we've had some experiences that led us to rethink. That's why bringing dogs to Haus Till E is unfortunately no longer possible. Thank you for your understanding.

accordion.title: Restrictions
accordion.content: Haus Till E is a listed building from the 1920s with no lift – the rooms are only accessible via the stairs. Smoking is not permitted inside the house, including on the balconies; you're welcome to smoke in our garden at any time.

accordion.title: Bicycles
accordion.content: You can safely park and charge your regular or electric bikes in our outbuilding. Prefer to rent locally? Our guests are particularly happy with the bike rentals at Wanderland (Balduinstraße 95) and Moselglück (Balduinstraße 43) – both offer well-maintained bikes right in Zell.

accordion.title: Air conditioning
accordion.content: Our historic house doesn't have classic air conditioning. On especially warm days, we're happy to bring a modern, bladeless tower fan (8 speed settings) to your room on request – just let us know.

accordion.title: Lactose, gluten, etc.
accordion.content: As a small, family-run house, we don't always have every product for every intolerance in stock as standard. Let us know your needs when booking – we're happy to accommodate you.

accordion.title: Family and children
accordion.content: Haus Till E is regularly booked by entire families – we've been lucky enough to witness many an 80th birthday and host three or four generations under one roof at the same time. We love creating the setting for unforgettable family time together.

accordion.title: Check-in and check-out times
accordion.content: Check-in is possible between 4 and 6 pm, check-out is by 11 am at the latest. We need the time in between to lovingly prepare and clean all five rooms for you. If you'd like to drop off your luggage earlier or collect the key in advance, just let us know ahead of time – we can usually find a solution.

text: Each of our five rooms is lovingly and uniquely furnished for you. On the second floor, two rooms with their own balcony await you (Rooms 1 & 2), as well as a spacious studio without a balcony (Room 3). On the third floor you'll find a large room with a wonderful view of the castle and the Moselle (Room 4), as well as a cosy room with charming sloped ceilings (Room 5).

Antique small furniture, original Art Deco globe lamps and real plants create an atmospheric feel in your room – complemented by exclusive artworks that an international artist created especially for each room. 'The rooms combine the luxury of the 1920s with all the comforts of the present' – that's how a guest once described it. A description we're very fond of.
Please note: our house has no lift – the rooms are only accessible via the stairs.

hosts.eyebrow: 03 — Your hosts look forward to welcoming you
text: We are Jan and René – and Haus Till E is our labour of love. The house has been around for many decades. When we first walked through its doors in April 2022, it was love at first sight: we instantly fell for this beautiful Art Deco estate – for the authentic stained-glass windows, the old wooden staircase and the idyllic garden, which Jan has lovingly tended ever since.

We moved from Berlin to the Moselle to find exactly what makes Zell so special: peace and quiet, fresh air, wide, hilly countryside, warm-hearted people, and the occasional glass of good Moselle wine. We'd love to share this love at first sight with you and get you just as excited about this wonderful 1920s building.
So we warmly invite you to be our guests.

At Haus Till E, everything revolves around what you secretly long for: peace to arrive, time to do nothing – and, if you wish, a little activity in between. From our favourite viewing bench (our personal 'Moselle cinema'), just a 10-minute walk from Haus Till E, you can watch the goings-on on the Moselle and simply let time drift by.

If you'd rather be active, you'll find hiking trails right on Haus Till E's doorstep such as the Liebesschlucht ('Lovers' Gorge', 11.1 km) or the Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km), relaxed cycling tours along the Moselle, or sportier stretches up into the steep vineyards of the 'Zeller Schwarze Katz'. And as a reward, more than 20 passionate winemakers as well as restaurants for every taste await you in Zell (Moselle) – from Greek to Asian, from ice cream sundaes to chocolate.

And if you look closely, you'll discover cultural hidden gems right at Haus Till E: classical concerts in the vaulted cellar, band performances in the garden, murder-mystery dinners with a multi-course menu – experiences you won't find on Google, only by being our guest.

accordion.title: Town
accordion.content: In town, we love strolling along the Moselle promenade and along Balduinstraße with its small shops and cafés. And from Kaimt, on the other side of the Moselle, you get the finest view of Zell's old town – with its towers, half-timbered houses and the more than 2,000-year-old winemaking history you can sense on every corner.

accordion.title: Countryside
accordion.content: Two very different landscapes meet around Zell: the Eifel and the Hunsrück. Here, wide views over gentle hills; there, dense forests with clearings that invite you to linger. A highlight in the Hunsrück is the Geierlay suspension bridge near Sosberg – at 360 metres long and up to 100 metres high, one of Germany's most spectacular suspension bridges, and pure adrenaline for anyone who isn't afraid of heights.

accordion.title: River
accordion.content: By boat, you can travel from Zell to Cochem, Beilstein, Traben-Trarbach or Bernkastel-Kues – past castles and vineyards, almost like passing through a model railway landscape. And since you can take your bikes on board, you can enjoy one leg comfortably by boat and cycle the other more actively – whichever you fancy.

accordion.title: Hills
accordion.content: At the foot of Haus Till E lies the famous steep vineyard 'Zeller Schwarze Katz' – and it is here, in the heart of the vineyard, that our house stands. Right behind Haus Till E starts the Collis circular trail (7.9 km, approx. 2 h 30 min, 210 metres of ascent) up to the Collis Tower, built in 1906, with a wonderful view over the town, and Merl and Briedel also offer hills with spectacular views. Just a 10-minute walk from Haus Till E lies our viewing bench, our very own 'Moselle cinema': from here you can watch the goings-on on the water and in the vineyards – the most beautiful and calming film nature has to offer.

accordion.title: Hiking
accordion.content: If you want to experience nature on foot, Haus Till E is the perfect base. The Liebesschlucht (11.1 km, moderate, approx. 3 h 15 min, 266 metres of ascent) takes you past the pilgrimage site of Marienhöhe through the forest down into a romantic rocky gorge. The Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km, moderate, approx. 4 h 35 min, 383 metres of ascent) rewards you with a detour to the Prinzenkopf tower and grand panoramic views of Germany's tightest Moselle loop. And the Collis circular trail (7.9 km, moderate, approx. 2 h 30 min, 210 metres of ascent) leads up to the historic Collis Tower with views over Zell and the Zeller Land. Three very different routes – all within easy reach of Haus Till E.

accordion.title: Cycling
accordion.content: Whether relaxed or sporty – Haus Till E has the right route for you. Right along the Moselle, the terrain is flat and gently sloping, ideal for a leisurely bike ride. If you prefer it more athletic, head up into the steep vineyards – short, sharp climbs included, rewarded with great views.

accordion.title: Wellness
accordion.content: About a 30-minute drive from Haus Till E lies the Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich – Germany's only Glauber's salt thermal spa, with a thermal pool, six saunas and a wide range of wellness treatments. A perfect trip whenever you're craving water, warmth and a little pampering.

accordion.title: Enjoying wine
accordion.content: More than 20 winemakers shape our Zeller Land with passion, professionalism and skill – producing excellent, multi-award-winning wines. In the steep vineyards, grapes are hand-picked with a love for the product you can taste. Our winemakers set trends, and the younger generation is bold enough to try new things. In numerous wine bars and vinotheques you can taste, sample and, of course, take the wines home with you.

accordion.title: Enjoying food
accordion.content: There's something for every taste: Greek at El Grego, Italian at Giovanni's, Indian at La Terrazza, German at Hotel zum Grünen Kranz, and Asian with top-notch sushi at Koi – all restaurants that have impressed with great quality for years. The best ice cream sundaes in town can be found at Stülb, Venezia or Perilli, the tastiest cakes at Café Stülb – and if you're after a sweet indulgence, head to DaKo, our Belgian chocolatier.

accordion.title: Enjoying culture
accordion.content: In the summer months, 'Summer in the City' awaits you – Thursday evenings with chill live music at changing locations in Zell, sometimes at a vineyard, sometimes right here in our garden at Haus Till E. From autumn to spring, we love heading to KulturKino Kaimt with its lovingly curated film programme. And in between, there are always small concerts at Haus Till E or with friends – in the garden, the living room, or the vaulted cellar, ranging from classical guitar to big band to minimalist electro beats, plus murder-mystery dinners with a multi-course menu. You'll find current dates on our events page.

items.title: How far is the viewing bench from Haus Till E?
items.content: The viewing bench, our "Moselle cinema", is a 10-minute walk from Haus Till E.

items.title: Which hiking trails start near Haus Till E?
items.content: Right on Haus Till E's doorstep begin the Collis circular trail (7.9 km), the Liebesschlucht (11.1 km) and the Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km).

items.title: How long and how difficult is the Marienburg circular trail?
items.content: The Marienburg circular trail is 15.2 km long, moderately difficult, and takes about 4 hours 35 minutes with 383 metres of ascent.

items.title: Where is Haus Till E located?
items.content: Haus Till E is located at the foot of the "Zeller Schwarze Katz" steep vineyard in Zell (Moselle), directly on the river.

items.title: How far is the Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich?
items.content: The Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich is about a 30-minute drive from Haus Till E.

items.title: How long is the Geierlay suspension bridge?
items.content: The Geierlay suspension bridge in the Hunsrück is 360 metres long and reaches up to 100 metres above the valley between Sosberg and Mörsdorf.

imprint.title: Imprint
imprint.intro: This website serves the private rental of a single apartment from one private individual to another. It is not operated commercially. We nevertheless voluntarily provide the following information for transparency.
imprint.liability_text: The content of this page has been prepared with care. However, no guarantee can be given for the accuracy, completeness and topicality of the information provided — in particular regarding the apartment. This page contains no links to external third-party websites.
imprint.dispute_text: As this page serves exclusively private rental purposes and does not constitute a commercial offer, the regulations on online dispute resolution (EU Commission's ODR platform) and consumer dispute resolution do not apply.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: The protection of your personal data is important to us. Below we inform you about which data is processed when you visit this website.
privacy.s2_p1: This website is provided via GitHub Pages (GitHub Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, USA, or its European group company). The domain is registered with Namecheap Inc. When you access the site, GitHub automatically processes technical information in so-called server log files transmitted by your browser. This typically includes the IP address, date and time of the request, the page accessed, the browser used, and the operating system.
privacy.s2_p2: This data is used exclusively for the technical operation, delivery of the website and protection against misuse. We do not combine it with other data sources. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in a secure and functional provision of the website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.s3_p1: The fonts used on this website (Fraunces, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono) are embedded locally. No connection is made to servers operated by Google or other third parties, and no data is transmitted to third parties.
privacy.s4_p1: This website does not use cookies or any tracking or analytics tools (e.g. Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, etc.). No user profiles are created.
privacy.s5_p1: If you contact us by email, the data you provide (e.g. name, email address, content of your message) will be stored by us in order to process your enquiry. We do not pass on this data without your consent.
privacy.s5_p2: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, provided your enquiry relates to the initiation of a rental agreement, or otherwise Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in processing your enquiry). The data will be deleted as soon as it is no longer required for processing, at the latest upon completion of the rental or final refusal.
privacy.s6_p1: For security reasons, this website uses SSL/TLS encryption. You can recognise an encrypted connection by the prefix https:// in your browser's address bar.
privacy.s7_intro: As a data subject, you have the following rights against us, provided the respective legal requirements are met:

Right to rectification of inaccurate data (Art. 16 GDPR)
Right to erasure of your data (Art. 17 GDPR)
Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
Right to object to processing (Art. 21 GDPR)
Right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, e.g. the authority responsible for your place of residence
